title: Finiteness of Perfect Squares in Factorial Sums

problemStatement.formal: Let A = {\sum_{n \in S} n! : S \subseteq \mathbb{N}, S finite}. Is A \cap {m^2 : m \in \mathbb{N}} finite? In the gallery notation, the target is (KthPowersInFactorialSums 2).Finite.
problemStatement.plain: Can a finite sum of distinct factorials equal a perfect square in infinitely many ways, or are there only finitely many such square-valued factorial sums? The gallery already proves the basic definitions and the example 1 = 0! = 1!.
whyMatters: Connects factorial-growth Diophantine equations with perfect powers and powerful numbers.
Targets a concrete Brindza-Erdos partial result that could be represented as an axiom or formalized if the needed number-theory bounds are available.
Exercises the existing Erdos1108Problem.lean infrastructure, which has definitions and small examples with no axioms or sorries.

proven: The gallery proof defines FactorialSums and KthPowersInFactorialSums and proves small example facts, including 1 as a square-valued factorial sum.
The local problem notes cite the Brindza-Erdos 1991 bound: for fixed r, a powerful number represented as a sum of r factorials has its largest factorial index bounded by a constant depending on r.
open: Whether (KthPowersInFactorialSums 2).Finite, the main perfect-square factorial-sum question, holds.
Whether the powerful factorial sums variant is finite.
Whether Mathlib contains enough Baker-type or p-adic valuation infrastructure to formalize the cited Brindza-Erdos bound rather than axiomatize it.
knownResults.goal: Determine whether the Brindza-Erdos bound can be formalized from available Mathlib tools, or isolate it as an axiom and derive finiteness consequences for square-valued factorial sums.

currentState.focus: Explore whether the Brindza-Erdos bound for powerful factorial sums can be formalized in Lean using the clean Erdos1108Problem.lean definitions.
currentState.nextAction: Read Proofs/Erdos1108Problem.lean, search Mathlib for factorial p-adic valuation tools, then decide whether to state a brindza_erdos_bound axiom and derive finiteness consequences.
